input.question: Why do computers freeze?
input.ground_truth: When you send a command to your computer (Like pressing on a button, clicking on your mouse or even moving it and so on) it enters a queue and your computer knows to read all of them according to the order they were sent. The reason for that is that some of the actions your computer makes cannot be interuptted and it has to wait until their completion. If that is the case, the queue is filling up and is not being read. Sometimes these actions are waiting for something to happen (like reading data from your hard-drive or finishing a calculation) and if for some reason this takes a long time (There can be many reasons for that, like a hardware problem, corrupt data, infinite loops etc) your computer will appear frozen.

Question: Why do computers freeze?

Okay! Imagine your computer is like a toy car.

When your toy car is running smoothly, it goes zoom zoom! But sometimes, if too many toys are in the way, or if the batteries are almost out, or if something gets stuck inside, your toy car might stop moving and just freeze.

A computer is a bit like that. It has lots of tiny jobs to do. Sometimes, too many jobs come at once, or a little part inside gets stuck, or it gets confused about what to do next. So, just like your toy car, the computer stops and doesn't move until you help it. That's called "freezing"!
